phases.goal: Use exact-prompt VLA to grasp or control the tabletrashbin body or rim, giving VLA enough continuous time to establish a stable bin relation without spilling contents early.
phases.name: vla_grasp_tabletrashbin
phases.verify: The tabletrashbin moves with the robot and remains recoverable.

phases.goal: Continue exact-prompt VLA from the current observed bin state to orient and pour the contents into the big bin or current task-language destination.
phases.name: vla_pour_contents
phases.verify: The balls leave the tabletrashbin toward the destination while the bin remains controlled.

semantic_recipe.relation_to_jsonl: Phases are transferable task guidance. The companion JSONL is a historical successful VLA-continuous trace; use it as evidence that this task benefits from giving exact-prompt VLA enough uninterrupted control time, not as literal replay.

strategy_notes.coordinate_policy: Relocalize all objects, supports, contacts, and poses from current observations; do not reuse clean coordinates.
critical_gates: The tabletrashbin is controlled before lift or tilt.
The balls are contents, not the grasp target.
The pour direction is based on current observation and destination, not a memorized pose.
If a VLA segment leaves a recoverable partial grasp, tilt, or pour state, re-observe and prefer another exact-prompt VLA continuation before changing control style.
A mid-sequence primitive can move the bin, balls, or receiving relation outside the physical continuity prepared by the previous VLA segment.
strategy_notes.language_policy: Stored task_language and companion JSONL prompts are historical source evidence. In any new episode, the current episode task language is authoritative; every new lingbot_act must use the complete current episode task language. Recipe text guides timing and chunk choice only; it never replaces the VLA prompt.

roles.destination: big bin or current task-language pour destination

task_language: Pick up the smooth tabletrashbin for small waste using the arm, pour balls.
vla_recipe: Exact sequence: 1:lingbot_act(chunks=8,use_length=50); 2:lingbot_act(chunks=4,use_length=50). For every lingbot_act, use the current episode complete task_language from state_00.json; the stored clean prompt in the companion JSONL is historical evidence only. Relocalize from current observations and do not replay clean coordinates. Treat this as a VLA-continuous recipe: after each segment, re-observe, then usually continue with short or medium exact-prompt VLA from the current physical state. If a segment is incomplete but still shows bin contact, grasp, tilt, or pour progress, give VLA enough continuation time to recover. Consider a primitive only as final local rescue or cleanup after several VLA continuations show no visible progress and the remaining blocker is narrow, local, and verifiable.

notes: Prefer continuous exact-prompt VLA for the grasp-and-pour sequence. Mid-sequence primitive intervention can leave the next VLA segment in an out-of-distribution physical state, so give VLA several observed continuation opportunities before final local rescue.
Primitive correction is best treated as cleanup for a narrow visible blocker after VLA continuity has stopped making progress, not as the main way to manipulate the bin or balls.
